We need produce demonstrations. We should include various configurations: top row markers + right column markers; bottom row + left column; top + left; bottom + right; cases where one border line has no marker -> unchanged; corners overlapping; etc. Also maybe all sides have markers? Verifier picks best pairing by score. We should show cases that reveal the selection logic. But student must infer. Simplicity: show clear cases.

Let's design inputs.

Note verifier: markers on edges. For a chosen edge_row (0 or h-1) and edge_col (0 or w-1), cols = markers at row==edge_row and col != edge_col. rows = markers at col==edge_col and row != edge_row. score = len(rows)*len(cols). Pick max score (first found with strict >, loops edge_row in {0,h-1}, edge_col in {0,w-1}). If tie, first wins: order edge_row 0, then h-1; edge_col 0 then w-1. So (0,0), (0,w-1), (h-1,0), (h-1,w-1).

If no markers at all -> untouched. If markers only on one border line (e.g., top row) and no column markers -> cols nonempty but rows empty => score 0 for all pairings -> best_score becomes 0 with first pairing (0,0) giving best_rows=[], best_cols= maybe columns except col 0. Then loops no rows -> no red. So unchanged. Good.

If markers only on left column -> rows nonempty, cols empty -> no red.

Corner markers: excluded from tallies for each pairing if c==edge_col for cols (i.e., marker at corner (edge_row, edge_col) excluded from cols), and r==edge_row for rows (same corner excluded). Other corner markers on same edge_row but not edge_col? They are columns. On edge_col but not edge_row, rows.

If both top and bottom rows have markers? Then choosing edge_row top vs bottom gives different columns. Score picks max. Similarly left/right columns.
